boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Jerusalem Plank Road record (June 21-24, 1864) in the Richmond-Petersburg Campaign [June 1864-March 1865]. The Wilson-Kautz raid records (VA113, VA067, VA068) begin on June 22 elsewhere; Lee's June 24 Hoke action is inside these dates. Army-wide returns, raid-wide and multi-action loss totals, and the siege as a whole are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.value: The frozen result reads 'Union gained ground' and the live result Union Victory, while the descriptions say the Second Corps was forced from the railroad but the siege lines were extended west. Lee says the enemy was driven from his first line to his second on June 22 and back from the railroad on June 23. Humphreys says the Second Corps re-established itself the next morning on the line it had been driven from, and the two armies stayed in that general position for some weeks.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The live 'Union Victory' and the frozen 'Union gained ground' are different categories; not reconciled.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 4,000 total and the live field 3,534 (US 2,962; CS 572). Humphreys gives the Second Corps loss as about 1,700 prisoners, four guns and several colors, with killed and wounded not severe; Lee reports about 1,600 prisoners, 4 guns and 8 colors on June 22, about 600 prisoners on June 23, and his own loss on June 24 as 97 killed and wounded and 209 missing.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The prisoner counts are captor and loser figures for overlapping populations.

open_questions: Birney's (No. 18), Barlow's, Gibbon's and Wright's reports, Meade's November 1 paragraph on June 21-23 (read, not selected), Hill's and Mahone's reports and the compiled returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff, later commander of its Second Corps, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan; it relies on Meade's, Hancock's, Warren's, Burnside's, Parke's and Wilson's reports and quotes Lee's, Beauregard's and Gordon's despatches, so it is not independent of those families. Gillmore's, Meade's, Hancock's, Burnside's, Wilson's, Hampton's, Stannard's and Lee's papers, printed in Official Records Series I, Volumes XXXVI (Part 2), XL, XLII and XLVI (Part 1), are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; each volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Lee's telegrams largely relay subordinates' reports. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
